packages.meaning: One function, decide(), takes the portfolio as it stood after yesterday and the market as of today's close, and returns what happened and what to do tomorrow. Backtest and live both call it.

The shared fill rule: next open, gap rules, slippage.

pair_reasons.engine>backtest: The engine is below the runners: it must not know who calls it.
pair_reasons.engine>live: The engine is below the runners: it must not know who calls it.
pair_reasons.engine>validation: The engine is below validation: it must not know who judges it.
pair_reasons.live>backtest: Live and backtest share only the engine, so they cannot differ in logic.
pair_reasons.validation>live: Validation judges results; it must not reach into the daily run.
pair_reasons.validation>strategies: Validation judges strategies from outside; it must not import one.
pair_reasons.backtest>live: A backtest must never touch the daily run.
pair_reasons.backtest>validation: Validation sits above backtest and reads its results.
pair_reasons.strategies>engine: A strategy never sees the engine: it only proposes. The one exception is the exit-policy interface types, so it can own an exit policy.
pair_reasons.strategies>risk: A strategy never sizes: sizing is shared.
pair_reasons.strategies>universe: A strategy never builds its own universe: eligibility is shared.
pair_reasons.strategies>live: A strategy never sees the live run or the portfolio.
pair_reasons.strategies>backtest: A strategy never sees the runner that calls it.
pair_reasons.strategies>validation: A strategy never sees how it is judged.
pair_reasons.strategies>config: A strategy cannot read or override the shared settings.
pair_reasons.strategies>data_checks: A strategy has nothing to do with the data checks.

strategy_rule.text: No strategy imports another strategy. Each one is built to run alone, so results are comparable and one cannot lean on another. A strategy may import one engine module, the exit-policy interface (stockbot.engine.exit_policy), so it can own its exit policy.

extra_rules.text: strategies may import stockbot.engine.exit_policy and nothing else from the engine (not the shared library stockbot.engine.exit_policies).
backtest, engine, strategies and risk may not import any network library.
engine and strategies may not import sqlite3 or sqlalchemy: they can never hold a database connection.
live importing validation is a temporary edge; it must disappear when the dashboard routers are reworked.

blocks.title: Data
blocks.plain: Prices, corporate actions and surveillance lists in one database, read only through a dated window.

blocks.title: Strategy
blocks.plain: Looks at today's close and proposes: a symbol and a stop. Nothing else. No strategy exists in the tree yet.

blocks.title: Engine and shared rules
blocks.plain: Decides who is eligible, how many shares, whether there is room, the fill, the stop and the costs. Same for every strategy.

blocks.title: Validation
blocks.plain: Counts every attempt and compares results with random entries. The pass rules are checked by a person: no code applies them yet (planned).

blocks.title: Backtest / Live runners
blocks.plain: Backtest replays history. Live runs the same step on the newest close. Both call decide().

blocks.title: Outputs / Tickets
blocks.plain: A ticket file of suggestions, and a state database. A person decides. Nothing is ever sent to a broker.

engine_steps.title: Check the inputs
engine_steps.plain: Is today the very next session after the state's date? If not, stop: decide() handles exactly one session.
engine_steps.example: State is at Day 1. Today is Day 2, the next session. Fine.
engine_steps.detail: Also checks: no duplicate strategy ids, and every exit policy named by a strategy or an open position is known.

engine_steps.title: Overlays
engine_steps.plain: Market-wide signals (such as an on/off switch) are evaluated once, before anything else. None exist yet.
engine_steps.out: Signals for the strategies that declared them
engine_steps.example: No overlay declared, so nothing to compute.
engine_steps.detail: A declared overlay that is missing or has the wrong version raises an error.

engine_steps.title: Fill yesterday's tickets
engine_steps.plain: Each ticket from yesterday fills at today's open plus slippage, unless a gap or a corporate action rules it out.
engine_steps.example: EXAMPLECO ticket, stop 190.00. Open 201.00, fill 201.40 (0.2% slippage). 877 shares.
engine_steps.detail: Shares are sized from the fill price, not the signal price. The reasons a ticket is not filled: no bar or already held, corporate action that day, gap through the stop, gap up too large.

engine_steps.title: Corporate actions
engine_steps.plain: A split or bonus today rescales each position's price and shares. Any other kind puts the position on HOLD.
engine_steps.out: Rescaled position, or a HOLD flag
engine_steps.example: Nothing today for EXAMPLECO. A 2-for-1 split would turn 877 shares at 201.40 into 1,754 at 100.70.
engine_steps.detail: The code does steps 4 and 5 together, one position at a time: actions first, then the bar.

engine_steps.title: Step through today's bar
engine_steps.plain: Each open position meets today's bar in a fixed order: pending exit at the open, stop against the low, then the exit policy may raise the stop.
engine_steps.out: Still open, or an exit and cash
engine_steps.example: Low 195.00 is above the stop 190.00, so EXAMPLECO stays open. Close 203.00.
engine_steps.detail: A position filled today is stepped through today's bar too, so a stop can be hit on the entry day. A stop never moves down.

engine_steps.title: Who is eligible?
engine_steps.plain: Shared rules decide which stocks a strategy may look at: not a fund, enough turnover, old enough, not under ASM/GSM.
engine_steps.example: EXAMPLECO: turnover well above the minimum, listed for years. Eligible.
engine_steps.detail: A strategy may make the list stricter, never looser. The code computes this per strategy, just before that strategy proposes.

engine_steps.title: Strategies propose
engine_steps.plain: Each strategy sees only the eligible list and the view. It returns proposals: symbol, reference price, stop.
engine_steps.example: A made-up strategy proposes EXAMPLECO: reference 203.00, stop 193.00. It cannot know the stock is already held.
engine_steps.detail: A proposal for a symbol not on the eligible list is blocked as NOT_ELIGIBLE.

engine_steps.title: Size it
engine_steps.plain: Shares equal the risk budget divided by the distance from entry to stop. The same formula for every strategy.
engine_steps.detail: Equity here is cash plus open positions after today's moves.

engine_steps.title: Arbitrate
engine_steps.plain: Proposals from all strategies meet one set of portfolio caps, in a fixed order. A symbol already held is refused.
engine_steps.out: Accepted or blocked, with a reason
engine_steps.example: EXAMPLECO is already held, so: blocked, ALREADY_HELD.
engine_steps.detail: Caps: number of positions, total portfolio risk %, sector exposure %.

engine_steps.title: Decisions and new State
engine_steps.plain: Everything that happened is packed into Decisions. Applying them to the old State gives tomorrow's State.
engine_steps.example: 1 fill, 0 exits, 0 new tickets, 1 blocked (ALREADY_HELD). One position carried forward.
engine_steps.detail: State is the fold of Decisions, so replaying the decisions rebuilds the state exactly.

backtest_lane.title: Choose window and start
backtest_lane.plain: A start date, an end date, starting equity and the strategies to run.
backtest_lane.detail: Called by tests or a research script. There is no strategy in the tree yet, so today only test strategies run.

backtest_lane.title: Lake read-only, no network
backtest_lane.plain: The database opens read-only and any network access during the run raises an error.
backtest_lane.detail: The guard patches the socket layer for the duration of the run.

backtest_lane.title: For each session: dated view
backtest_lane.plain: For each trading day, build a view that cannot show anything later than that day.
backtest_lane.detail: Asking for a bar after the date raises FutureDataError.

backtest_lane.title: Close what is open at the end
backtest_lane.plain: At the end of the window, any open position is closed so every trade has a result.
backtest_lane.detail: Then the result is returned with every Decisions object.

backtest_lane.title: Result and manifest
backtest_lane.plain: A BacktestResult, plus a manifest: config hash, strategy hashes, git SHA.
backtest_lane.detail: The manifest is what lets someone reproduce the run later.

live_lane.title: Mode gate
live_lane.plain: PAPER by default. LIVE needs a strategy with status live and a validation reference.
live_lane.detail: With an empty book, a daily run produces no tickets by design.

live_lane.title: Is today's data there?
live_lane.plain: Refuses to run if the day's prices are not in the lake yet (DataFreshnessError).
live_lane.detail: Nothing in the repository appends new sessions to the lake today; see DATA_GUIDE section I.

live_lane.title: Load the ASM/GSM list
live_lane.plain: Reads the day's surveillance snapshot. LIVE mode fails closed if it is missing.
live_lane.detail: Raises SurveillanceDataMissing in LIVE; PAPER continues without it.

live_lane.title: Operator reports first
live_lane.plain: The operator's real fills and exits are applied before the engine thinks, because reality overrides the guess.

live_lane.title: Journal it
live_lane.plain: Decisions go into an append-only journal. Running the same date again changes nothing.
live_lane.detail: rebuild() must equal load(): the journal is the truth.

live_lane.title: Write the ticket file
live_lane.plain: One file per session: state/tickets/tickets_<date>.json, with tickets, blocked items and flags.
live_lane.detail: The file says: suggestions for the operator, nothing is sent to any broker.

live_lane.title: A person reads and reports back
live_lane.plain: The operator decides whether to act, and reports real fills and exits for the next run.
live_lane.detail: This is the only human step in the loop.

shared_box.title: decide()
shared_box.plain: The same function in both lanes.
shared_box.detail: Backtest calls it in strict mode (errors stop the run). Live calls it with strict off and mode live, so one broken strategy is flagged instead of stopping the day. Otherwise the decisions must be identical: tests/unit/test_engine_live.py compares them day by day.

trade_steps.title: Proposed
trade_steps.plain: A strategy proposes a symbol with a reference price and a stop. It is only an idea.

trade_steps.title: Sized and capped
trade_steps.plain: Shared code sizes it and checks the portfolio caps. If it does not fit, it is Blocked and recorded.
trade_steps.example: 1,000 shares. Caps: room for one more position. Accepted.

trade_steps.title: Ticket
trade_steps.plain: An accepted proposal becomes a ticket and waits one night in the State.
trade_steps.example: Ticket sits in State.pending until the next open.

trade_steps.title: Filled at the next open
trade_steps.plain: Filled at the open plus entry slippage. A gap through the stop, or too big a gap up, drops it (NotFilled).
trade_steps.example: Open 205.00, fill 205.41 with 0.2% slippage. Buy costs are charged.

trade_steps.title: Stepped on the same bar
trade_steps.plain: A new position is stepped through its entry bar at once, so the stop can be hit on day one.
trade_steps.example: Entry-day low 199.00 is above the stop 193.00. Still open.

trade_steps.title: Stop moves up
trade_steps.plain: Each session the exit policy may raise the stop. A stop can never move down.
trade_steps.example: Stop raised 193.00 to 198.00 after a good week.

trade_steps.title: Exit
trade_steps.plain: The stop is hit, a limit fills, or a market exit goes out at the next open. Exit slippage and sell costs apply.
trade_steps.example: Stop 198.00 hit. Fill at min(open, stop) less 0.2% exit slippage.

trade_steps.title: Closed trade
trade_steps.plain: A ClosedTrade record: gross profit, costs, net profit and R (profit divided by the amount risked).

trade_side_states.title: Blocked
trade_side_states.plain: Not eligible, sizing fails, or caps are full. Recorded with a reason.

trade_side_states.title: Not filled
trade_side_states.plain: Gap through the stop, gap up too large, corporate action that day, already held, or no bar.

trade_tags.caps: Portfolio caps apply here: positions, total risk %, sector %.
trade_tags.cost: Trading costs are charged here (STT, fees, stamp duty, GST, DP charge).

add_items.title: Strategy file
add_items.plain: A new module in stockbot/strategies/ that imports only the interface.
skeleton: # stockbot/strategies/<your_id>.py  (a NEW file, one strategy per file)
# import ONLY: Proposal from stockbot.strategies.base, StrategySpec from stockbot.strategies.spec
# class with:
#   propose(view, eligible, as_of, strategy_state, overlays) -> (list of Proposal, new strategy_state)
#   confirm_fill(proposal, fill_price, view) -> None to accept, or a reason string
# Its memory lives in strategy_state (plain data), never in an attribute.
# It must NOT: open a database, read the clock, import another strategy, size positions.

add_items.title: StrategySpec
add_items.plain: The strategy's identity card: id, version, own parameters, exit policy, status.
skeleton: # SPEC = StrategySpec(id=..., version=..., params={...}, exit_policy=..., status=...)
# id: lower-case, 2 to 40 characters.  version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
# params: only the strategy's OWN settings; shared sections (costs, portfolio_risk ...) are rejected
# status: research, paper or live. live is refused without validation_ref
# config_hash(): any change to any field changes the hash, and the hash goes in the ledger

add_items.title: Exit policy
add_items.plain:
How the stop moves and when to ask for an exit. Pick a shared one by id (fixed_hold_ or trailing_pct_

) in StrategySpec.exit_policy, or write your own inside your strategy folder.
skeleton: # Shared library (stockbot/engine/exit_policies): just name it in the spec, nothing to write:
#   exit_policy="fixed_hold_20"   exit at the open of session 21 (the entry session is session 1)
#   exit_policy="trailing_pct_10" stop trails 10% below the highest close since entry
# Your own policy: a class in stockbot/strategies/<your_id>/ that imports ONLY the interface types from
#   stockbot.engine.exit_policy (never stockbot.engine.exit_policies or another engine module), with:
#   initial_state(position, view), step(position, bar, view, ctx) -> PolicyActions, on_corporate_action(exit_state, factor)
#   and pass it to policies_for(specs, extra=[policy]); its id must not start with fixed_hold_ or trailing_pct_.
# The policy decides WHAT; the engine's step_position decides HOW, in one fixed order. A stop can never move down.

add_items.title: Registry line
add_items.plain: One line that registers the spec. Duplicate ids are rejected.
skeleton: # default_registry.register(SPEC)
# rejects a duplicate id; today the registry is empty
# tests/unit/test_no_strategy_in_the_tree.py will (rightly) fail: that tripwire is a reviewed decision

add_items.title: Pre-registration
add_items.plain: Write down the configurations and the pass rules, and hash them, before looking at any result.
skeleton: # 1. list the configurations and gate parameters in pre_registered_configs.yaml
# 2. register(ledger=..., yaml_path=..., gate_params=..., candidate_ids=..., git_sha=...)
# 3. the number of attempts is now fixed in the hash-chained trial ledger
# Rows are only ever appended; an edited row breaks the chain.

add_items.title: Tests
add_items.plain: Tests for the new strategy, and the existing guards must stay green.
skeleton: # a new tests/unit/test_<your_id>.py on a synthetic lake (tests/fixtures/)
# must stay green: test_import_boundaries.py, test_strategy_spec.py, test_engine_decide.py
# a failing test is fixed in the code, never by editing an expected value

never_items.title: shared.yaml
never_items.plain: Costs, risk limits, universe rules and gates are shared. A strategy cannot override them.
never_items.why: Otherwise two strategies could not be compared.

never_items.title: engine, risk, universe
never_items.plain: Fills, stops, sizing, caps and eligibility are shared code.
never_items.why: One rule set for every strategy and for the random baseline.

never_items.title: Ledger rows
never_items.plain: Rows are only appended, never edited.
never_items.why: The count of attempts is the evidence.

never_items.title: finsight.db
never_items.plain: The price database is opened read-only. Tests prove it is unchanged.
never_items.why: G4 compares its hash and modified time.

never_items.title: Import rules
never_items.plain: Do not edit the rule table to make an import pass.

never_items.title: Another strategy
never_items.plain: No strategy imports or reads another strategy.
never_items.why: Each strategy must be judged alone.

validation_steps.title: Pre-register
validation_steps.q: What exactly are we testing, and what counts as a pass?
validation_steps.plain: Configurations and gates are written down before any result is seen.

validation_steps.title: Hash lock
validation_steps.q: Can the plan be changed afterwards without anyone noticing?
validation_steps.plain: prereg_lock hashes the yaml and the gate parameters.

validation_steps.title: Trial ledger
validation_steps.q: How many attempts have been made?
validation_steps.plain: Every attempt is a row in a hash-chained ledger. Dry runs count too (record_exploratory).

validation_steps.title: Backtest
validation_steps.q: What would it have done in history?
validation_steps.plain: Each registered configuration runs through the same engine.

validation_steps.title: Matched-random baseline
validation_steps.q: Is it better than random entries under identical rules?
validation_steps.plain: Random entries matched to each real trade, run through the same fills, stops and costs.

validation_steps.title: Paired weekly advantage
validation_steps.q: By how much, week by week?
validation_steps.plain: Strategy minus random, paired by week.

validation_steps.title: Max-T bootstrap
validation_steps.q: After trying K configurations, is the best one still real?
validation_steps.plain: A bootstrap across all K configurations that adjusts for having tried several.

validation_steps.title: Gates
validation_steps.q: Does it clear the pass rules?
validation_steps.plain: validation_gates are settings only. No code applies them yet (planned); a person compares.

validation_steps.title: Status
validation_steps.q: May it run, and in which mode?
validation_steps.plain: A person sets StrategySpec.status and validation_ref. No code promotes a strategy.

symptoms.tip: fill_ticket: open times (1 + entry slippage), gap rules. Then compare raw and adjusted bars.

symptoms.symptom: A stop was hit when it should not have been (or the reverse)
symptoms.tip: The stop is checked against the bar's low, entry bar included. Check for a corporate action that day.

symptoms.symptom: A symbol is missing from the eligible list
symptoms.tip: Fund, turnover, listing age, ASM/GSM. Did it trade that day? The lake holds the EQ series only.

symptoms.symptom: Prices jump as if there were an error
symptoms.tip: Look at corporate_actions_log for that symbol and ex-date (DATA_GUIDE section E).
DataFreshnessError: the date is not in the lake yet. ModeError: LIVE with no live strategy. An empty book means no tickets by design.
Exit code 2: mode, freshness, or a missing ASM/GSM snapshot in LIVE.
StateStore.rebuild() must equal load(). Table journal in state/live_state.db.

symptoms.symptom: A ticket is missing from the file
symptoms.tip: blocked and flags in state/tickets/tickets_<date>.json give a reason for each blocked proposal.

symptoms.symptom: A number differs between backtest and live
symptoms.tip: They must not. The test compares decisions day by day; only mode and strict differ.

symptoms.symptom: An import is refused by the build
symptoms.tip: See the Who can import whom view. Never edit the table to pass.
It is env-gated: STOCKBOT_DATA_TESTS=1 (real database) or STOCKBOT_FINAL_CHECK=1.

glossary.def: One trading day. The calendar is the dates of the Nifty 50 series in the lake.
The date a question is asked from. An AsOfView answers as the world looked at that day's close, and refuses to show later data.
Average daily traded value: raw close times raw volume, averaged over 20 sessions, in rupees.
The amount risked on a trade: shares times (entry minus initial stop). A profit of 2R is twice the amount risked.
The first day a stock trades without the right to a corporate action such as a split or bonus.
Admitting proposals from several strategies against one set of portfolio caps in a fixed order. A symbol already held is refused.
Pre-registration: writing the configurations and pass rules down, and hashing them, before looking at results.
The append-only record of every attempt, hash-chained so an edit is detectable.
A suggestion for the operator: symbol, planned shares, reference price, stop. Created at one close, filled in the simulation at the next open.
Point-in-time: using only what was knowable on the as-of date. A single current snapshot, such as today's share count, is not PIT.
NSE's ordinary equity segment. The lake holds EQ rows only, so a name in another segment shows up as a long absence.
A shared signal evaluated once before everything else, such as a market-wide switch. None exists yet.
A position the engine cannot rescale after a corporate action (merger, demerger, rights). It is flagged and left out of trade statistics.
NSE's Additional and Graded Surveillance Measures lists. A name on today's list is excluded.
finsight.db, the price database. Opened read-only by all decision code.
The whole portfolio memory after a session: cash, open positions, pending tickets.
What happened in one session: fills, exits, new tickets, blocked items, flags. State is the fold of Decisions.
A pure function has no database, network, clock or randomness of its own: the same inputs always give the same outputs.
Running it again with the same input changes nothing.
The assumed gap between the price you expect and the price you get, applied on entry and on exit.
The price at which a position is sold to limit the loss. It may be raised, never lowered.
The rule for moving the stop and asking for exits. The policy decides what; the engine decides how.
A strategy's identity card: id, version, parameters, exit policy, status. Its hash goes in the ledger.
decide(strict=True): any error stops the run (backtest). strict=False flags it and carries on (live).
A bootstrap that adjusts for having tried several configurations, so the best of K is not over-trusted.
Random entries matched to each real trade and run through identical rules: what luck alone would have earned.
One of the named test groups G1 to G6 used to prove nothing drifted.
A test that is skipped unless an environment variable is set, because it needs the real database or takes minutes.
NSE's end-of-day price file for all listed securities.
A split, bonus, dividend, merger or similar event. Splits and bonuses adjust prices; others put an open position on HOLD.
The dated window onto the lake. The only way code above the data layer reads market data.
The default mode: the daily run produces suggestions only and no strategy needs to be live.
Allowed by the shared universe rules: not a fund, enough turnover, old enough, not under ASM/GSM.
Three portfolio limits: number of positions, total risk %, and sector exposure %.
The list of registered strategies. Empty today.
